author: ojiudezue
title: Arrival wording: 'arrived' only with the person's own arrival edge, else 'came in'; unified room rules built
summary: The first live named arrivals came from the old single-face path, and one was wrong: 'Jaya arrived' while she had been home 46 minutes and walked in from the garage. The operator chose both fixes: say 'arrived' only when the named person's own counted arrival edge falls in the S1 window, otherwise 'came in' for a resident already home. S1 also failed to anchor a correct case at 12:39 for an unrecorded reason, so every non-anchor now records its reason. Separately, unified room rules (AI-ROOM-RULES-TRUST-REPAIR-1 D1-D9) was built and awaits review.
why: A face match proves who walked through a door, not that they just came home; the phone's own arrival edge is the independent evidence of arriving. Without reject reasons the S1 yield gap could not be diagnosed.
alternatives_considered: Gate only (no notice for home residents)
Reword only ('came in' for all face entries)
implications: Entry notices now encode F1 (arriving) separately from F3 (crossing) in their wording. The 12:39 gap is expected to be the plan's synthetic-face exclusion; the next crossing's edge_anchor_reason confirms it.
revisit_trigger: edge_anchor_reason shows a gate firing on correct arrivals, or a 'came in' for someone who actually arrived
